newsitem.title: GERMANY: BME/Reuters index shows German growth gaining pace.
newsitem.headline: BME/Reuters index shows German growth gaining pace.

text.p: Germany's manufacturing sector grew at an accelerated pace in April but employment continued to fall, according to a new indicator launched by Reuters Holdings Plc and the BME managers' association.

The BME/Reuters German Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), first published on Tuesday and available exclusively on Reuters systems, showed that the sector expanded faster in April than it did in any month since the survey started one year ago.

The PMI rose to a seasonally-adjusted 56.58 in April from 54.58 in March, reaching the highest level yet recorded. On an unadjusted basis, the index also hit a record of 57.93, up from 56.43 in March.
The PMI, modelled on the closely watched U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index, reveals growing evidence that capacity shortages are emerging in Europe's largest economy.
It also shows inflationary pressures mounting amid lengthening delivery times and rising import prices.

"These figures confirm the anecdotal evidence that we are getting from the companies we cover and makes us more confident in our forecast that the German economy is set for quite a sharp jump in the second quarter," said Larry Anderson, head of research at Bayerische Vereinsbank.

The release of the April PMI coincided with data suggesting the economy will pick up pace in the second quarter while disappointing unemployment figures showed the labour market remained in the doldrums in April.
Seasonally adjusted unemployment rose by 8,000 people to 4.347 million while the unadjusted unemployment rate fell to 11.3 pct from 11.7 percent -- a smaller decline than usual at this time of year.

Meanwhile German industry orders in March rose 1.1 percent from the previous month, confirming the economy is growing faster than expected and suggesting that gross domestic product will grow one percent in the second quarter, analysts said.
They also noted that while exports remained the driving force behind the current upturn, domestic demand for plant and equipmnent was beginning to pick up.
That trend was underlined by the April PMI data.

"Purchasing managers have reported that the weaker exchange rate has helped boost sales on foreign markets in recent months, but a revival in demand from the domestic market was the main cause of a further acceleration in the rate of growth in April," NTC said in a statement.
But the pace of growth was not sufficient to prevent further job losses and employment continued to fall in April, as it has done throughout the survey's history, NTC said.

The PMI, based on a survey of 350 managers carried out exclusively for Reuters by research group NTC Publications Ltd, is designed to provide an overall view of activity in the manufacturing sector and acts as a leading indicator.
The survey is carried out in cooperation with the BME German Federation for Materials Management, Purchasing and Logistics and will be published on the first working day of each month.
The PMI is derived from individual diffusion indices which measure changes in output, new orders, employment, suppliers' delivery times and stocks of goods purchased.

A reading below 50 percent indicates that the manufacturing economy is generally declining, while a level above 50 percent shows it generally expanding. The more it deviates from 50, the greater the improvement or decline in the current month.
Purchasing managers are viewed as valuable sources as they tend to have access to information denied to other managers.

Their assessment of new orders is assigned the greatest weight in the PMI because orders tend to lead the economic cycle. In April, the German PMI's new orders index rose to a seasonally-adjusted 60.39 from 58.58.
Mike Waterson, chairman of NTC Research, said the PMI complemented the Ifo institute's business climate index.
"The two surveys are complementary. Taken together they should provide a better view of the German economy," Waterson told the news conference.
Copyright in the BME/Reuters Purchasing Managers' Index is owned by Reuters Limited.
NTC also plans to launch a service sector index for Germany. This would, in conjunction with the manufacturing index, allow early assessments of GDP.
